To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

exposure of EHEC to CM from HCT- 8 cells increases EHEC virulent gene expression and EHEC adherence to epithelial cells, and that the host-derived molecules that mediate these changes are protein(s) with molecular mass greater than 3 kDA.

exposure to human intestinal epithelial cell-conditioned medium increases the expression of virulence genes in EHEC, which in turn leads to increased attachment of the bacteria to intestinal epithelial cells.
human intestinal epithelial cell-secreted protein(s) increase the expression of EHEC virulent genes and phage titers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism by which the host cell can increase EHEC attachment and virulence gene expression.
the effect that human intestinal cell-derived molecule(s), which increase the expression of EHEC virulent genes and phage titer, has on EHEC virulence.
host factors that may influence EHEC infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the host cell-derived protein(s) in the CM from HCT-9 intestinal epithelial cell line increase EHEC adherence and virulence gene expression in EHEC.
HCT-8 cell-derived protein(s) increase EHEC adherence to epithelial cells and virulence gene expression.
host cell-derived protein-based molecule(s) increase EHEC attachment and virulence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HCT-8 epithelial cell-derived protein(s) increase EHEC attachment, phage expression and Shiga toxin production.
host cell-derived protein(s) increase EHEC attachment by up-regulating EHEC virulent gene expression.
human intestinal epithelial cells produce a protein-based molecule(s) that increases EHEC virulences and attachment to epithelial cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
human intestinal epithelial cells secrete a molecule(s) that increases the expression of LEE and 933W prophages and enhances EHEC attachment.
host cell-derived molecules increase the virulence of EHEC.
human intestinal epithelial cells produce molecule(s) that can enhance the virulence of EHEC.
